data.title: Tesla Model 3 outsold the BMW 5 Series two to one in South Korea last month
data.description:
The Tesla Model 3 is closing in on the BMW 5 Series for second place among South Korea’s best-selling imported sedans, after Tesla again topped the country’s import market in October.

According figures from Korea’s import car association, KAIDA, there’s a three-way fight in the country’s imported sedan market this year.

The Mercedes-Benz E-Class is still out in front, with 21,034 registrations from January through October. The 5 Series follows at 18,917, and the Model 3 is third at 15,459.(via Seoul Economic Daily)

October was a strong month for Tesla’s sedan, and that is what has tightened the race for second. It registered 3,553 cars, more than double the 1,478 the 5 Series put up in the same month.

Even so, the BMW still leads by 3,458 cars for the year so far. The report said that if October’s pace holds, the Model 3 could pass it by year end.

The Model 3 is actually closer in size to a Mercedes C-Class or a BMW 3 Series than to these larger cars. On the sales charts, though, it is now running with the E-Class and the 5 Series.

The E-Class has long been the usual choice among imported mid-size sedans, and it remains well ahead in first place. The 5 Series nudged ahead in the first half of the year, then Mercedes came back with two strong months in the fall.

Tesla’s record year in South Korea

Tesla is having a record year in South Korea. It became the country’s top imported car brand for the first time in the opening quarter, then held that lead from February onward, including a record 13,190 registrations in April. It registered 89,148 vehicles through the first nine months, about a third of the entire import market.

The Model Y has done most of the heavy lifting, and in several months it even outsold every other vehicle in the country. Sales eased in October to 9,165, ending a seven-month run above 10,000, though Tesla still finished first among importers.

data.title: Tesla Opens First Tesla Semi Service Centre in Laredo, Texas
data.description:
Tesla has opened its first dedicated Tesla Semi Service Centre located in Laredo, Texas. The company held an event at the site on Friday, featuring Tesla Semi ride-alongs and a tour of the new facility.

The facility is located at 13505 Regional Drive in Laredo and is located off Interstate 35. This location is no accident; it sits just off Interstate 35, one of the busiest commercial trucking corridors in the country.

Laredo sits on the border with Nuevo Leon in Mexico, and this specific port of entry handles the most land-based trade in the United States.

Multiple key Tesla suppliers are just over the border from Laredo, including Quanta Computer, Noah Itcech, Brembo, and AGP Group.

It does look like Tesla is on the cusp of opening its second service centre in the state. Many Tesla insiders are expecting that a recent lease of a 30,000-square-foot facility in Buda, Texas, just south of Austin, will be the second dedicated Tesla Semi Service Centre.

However, Tesla has not officially confirmed what it is using this newly leased property for.

If Tesla rolls out Megachargers and dedicated Tesla Semi Service Centres over the next few months, it will most likely be in a service triangle that was publicly discussed back in 2025.

This service triangle runs from Austin to San Antonio and finally to El Paso. So, following the trend, we should see the next rumoured or confirmed site to be somewhere in West Texas.

data.title: Tesla Cybercab Purchase Agreement Reveals Strict Ownership and Operating Restrictions
data.description:
Tesla has outlined strict ownership and operating conditions for its Cybercab, revealing new restrictions for customers invited to purchase the autonomous vehicle for US$29,990.

According to screenshots of Tesla’s purchase and Autonomy Subscription agreements shared by Spencer (@scotsrule08) on X, owners must maintain an active subscription, currently priced at US$299 per month, or their Cybercab will not operate.

The documents also give Tesla considerable control over how customers use, modify, transfer, and even retain ownership of their vehicles.

Resale and Buyback Terms

Under the purchase agreement, owners cannot sell or transfer their Cybercab without Tesla’s written permission. Unauthorized transactions carry contractual damages of at least US$50,000, or the full transaction value if higher.

Tesla also reserves the right to repurchase a Cybercab at any time, at a fair market value determined by the company. Owners must cover the cost of returning the vehicle.

Subscription Terms

Meanwhile, the subscription agreement limits Cybercab operation to Tesla-approved geographic areas, which the company can expand or reduce. Commercial activities, including ride-hailing and rentals, require separate authorization.

The subscription covers autonomous driving, connectivity, roadside assistance, and selected maintenance services, including tires, windshields, wipers, cabin filters, and camera cleaning.

Fees and Enforcement

However, owners remain responsible for insurance, charging, registration, and other expenses. Modifications such as wraps, window tinting, and wheel changes must also go through Tesla or authorized providers.

The agreement further specifies that three or more strikeouts for improper or unsafe use trigger a one-week suspension of autonomous driving, without a subscription refund.

Tesla can also remotely restrict or disable vehicle operation. Subscription pricing may change with one month’s notice.

The restrictions accompany Tesla’s plans to deliver its first customer Cybercabs by the end of 2026.

data.title: Tesla invites select customers to buy Cybercab for $29,990 – with $299 monthly ‘autonomy fee’
data.description:
Tesla has taken the first step in their promise to deliver a Cybercab to customers in 2026. On Friday the company announced select customers are now being invited to purchase a Cybercab for personal use.

The announcement also included the price for a personal Cybercab – just US$29,990, with December 2026 showing as a delivery estimate.

While that price is low, there is also an ongoing cost beyond purchasing the vehicle – a mandatory autonomy subscription.

The company’s Robotaxi account announced the invitations on X, sharing a copy of the customer email describing a limited initial release, with operation restricted to supported service areas. Since Cybercab is currently only available in Austin, we are presuming only buyers in that market are being targeted in this initial wave, and not in the other areas where Tesla operates its Robotaxi service.

Monthly subscription required

Perhaps the biggest reveal with the announcement is that customers buying a Cybercab for personal use will have to pay a new “Autonomy Subscription.” It isn’t cheap either at US$299 per month – but Tesla is including the first month for free.

That is significantly higher than the US$99 per month Tesla owners currently pay for the Full Self-Driving (FSD) subscription, and could offer a clue to how Tesla might price Unsupervised FSD for owners’ vehicles when that day arrives.

The terms state that operating the vehicle requires not only the subscription, but also regular maintenance. Buyers placing an order must also pay a US$1,000 deposit that cannot be refunded.

Tesla meets its Cybercab price target

At US$29,990, Tesla has matched the target price Musk outlined when Cybercab debuted in October 2024. Musk reaffirmed the sub-US$30,000 target in February, along with plans to deliver vehicles to customers before 2027. The new price meets that commitment, while the December delivery estimate lines up with the original timeline.

That also puts tech reviewer Marques Brownlee’s (MKBHD) hair back in the spotlight. After the 2024 unveiling, MKBHD promised to shave his head on camera if Tesla made Cybercab available to customers for US$30,000 before 2027. With invitations now going out at US$29,990 and deliveries estimated for December, Tesla is getting close to making him follow through.

data.title: United touts Starlink competitive advantage as rollout accelerates
data.description:
United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby says Starlink is giving the carrier its biggest competitive advantage in a century, as the airline accelerates its rollout of the technology.

Speaking at Yahoo Finance Invest this week, Kirby said passengers are choosing United specifically to try SpaceX’s satellite internet, and he believes the service is already contributing to revenue.

“I think it’s the biggest near-term competitive advantage that we’ve ever had in United’s 100-year history. Eventually everyone’s going to have a competitive product, but we have a huge lead,” Kirby said. (via Yahoo)

According to United’s Starlink tracker, the airline now has 697 Starlink-equipped aircraft, representing 46% of its fleet, and 21 more aircraft than 10 days ago.

United is of course not the only airline targeting an aggressive Starlink rollout. American Airlines plans to begin equipping more than 1,000 mainline aircraft in early 2027. Southwest is targeting completion across its fleet by fall 2027.

Then others are going a different route. Delta has chosen Amazon Leo for an initial 500 aircraft, with installations only starting in 2028. Kirby questioned that choice, saying, “I think Leo is a mistake,” while also praising Delta’s broader business.

United expects Starlink availability to approach 64% of daily flights before year-end. The airline also recently announced it is accelerating its installation schedule, with the original two-to-three-year deployment timeline reduced to 18 months.

data.title: Lucid Offers $10,000 Credit in Canada, $15,000 U.S. Black Friday Deal
data.description:
Lucid is offering Canadian buyers up to C$10,000 in credits and 0% financing on select 2026 vehicles, while customers south of the border are getting a separate Black Friday deal on the updated 2027 Gravity Touring and Air Touring.

According to Lucid’s Canadian offers page, the 2026 Air Touring is listed at C$112,800, with buyers able to take advantage of a C$10,000 credit and 0% financing for up to 72 months through Lucid Financial Services.

The less expensive 2026 Air Pure is also eligible for 0% financing, along with a C$7,500 credit.

For those interested in an SUV, Lucid is offering up to C$10,000 toward a 2026 Gravity purchased with cash. Buyers who finance or lease instead can receive a C$7,500 credit, along with a 0.99% interest rate.

Lucid is also throwing in a C$4,000 allowance for qualifying trade-ins and a C$1,000 test-drive credit. However, the company’s Canadian website has conflicting terms for the test-drive offer, and may not be stackable with every other incentive.

These Canadian offers require qualifying deliveries by November 30, and the Lucid Credit does not apply to the 2027 Gravity.

Bigger Black Friday credits in the U.S.

Meanwhile, Lucid is offering American buyers even larger credits as part of a separate Black Friday promotion.

According to an early-access email sent customers this week, they can receive US$15,000 (C$21,272) toward a 2027 Gravity Touring or US$10,000 (C$14,181) toward a 2027 Air Touring. (via Reddit)

Both offers are US$5,000 (C$7,091) higher than the regular cash credits currently advertised on Lucid’s U.S. website.

There is a catch, however. The Black Friday credits are only available to customers purchasing with cash or third-party financing. Customers financing or leasing through Lucid Financial Services aren’t eligible.

The credits also can’t be combined with other incentives or discounts, and the promotion runs through November 30.

Incentives follow disappointing Q3 sales

The latest offers also come as Lucid tries to improve sales following a disappointing third quarter.

Lucid delivered just 3,806 vehicles during Q3 2026, down 4% from the previous quarter and 7% compared to the same period last year. The results also fell short of Wall Street expectations of 4,687 deliveries.

Production took an even bigger hit, falling 38% from Q2 to just 2,954 vehicles. However, much of that decline was intentional, with Lucid cutting production to reduce its inventory of unsold vehicles and improve cash flow.

data.title: Global EV Sales Return to Growth in October, Reaching 2.09 Million
data.description:
Global electric vehicle (EV) sales have returned to annual growth in October following a decline in September, with stronger demand in Europe and other markets helping offset weaker sales in China.

According to Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, global sales of battery-electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids reached 2.09 million units, up 8% year-over-year but down 3% from September.

Year-to-date sales reached 17.5 million vehicles, representing a 5% increase compared to the same period in 2025 (via Reuters).

Europe continued to lead growth among established EV markets, with sales increasing 36% year-over-year to 510,000 vehicles. Battery-electric sales climbed 49%, while plug-in hybrids rose 7%.

Meanwhile, North American EV sales increased 24% year-over-year to 130,000 units, marking the region’s first annual increase of 2026. However, the improvement reflects a weaker comparison period.

The U.S. federal EV tax credit expired in September 2025, leaving October as the first month compared against a period without the incentive.

China remained the largest EV market by far, recording 1.14 million sales despite a 12% annual decline. Sales nevertheless increased 5% compared to September.

Sales outside China, Europe and North America climbed 85% to 300,000 vehicles, exceeding North America’s total. Chinese passenger vehicle new energy vehicle exports reached almost 600,000 units in October, another monthly record.

data.title: Canada’s EV Market Share Climbs From 7% to 13% in 18 Months
data.description:
Canada’s electric vehicle (EV) market share, at 13% in August 2026, has nearly doubled from a year and a half earlier, after remaining virtually unchanged in the second quarter.

The new figures come from the Canadian Climate Institute, showing EV market share has climbed from a low of 7% in February 2025, following a sharp decline in sales caused by a rollback in government support.

Canada’s EV market continues to recover

The figures were released Thursday alongside the launch of the Climate Progress Tracker, a new interactive tool built by the Institute’s 440 Megatonnes project to monitor Canada’s transition to cleaner energy. The tracker measures EV market share using new battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicle sales as a percentage of all new light-duty vehicle sales.

A total of 22,716 new zero-emission vehicles were sold in August, representing 13.0% of the market, up from 8.8% a year earlier.

The recovery also follows the return of federal EV rebates in February 2026, offering buyers up to $5,000 toward eligible vehicles.

Clean energy and battery storage see strong growth

Beyond EV sales, the tracker uses more than 40 indicators across five categories: the clean economy, electrification, clean energy, industrial performance, and emissions progress.

Among its findings, Canada’s wind and solar capacity has increased by nearly 7 gigawatts since 2020, representing growth of more than 40%.

Battery storage capacity has also increased more than sixfold over the same period, reaching almost 900 megawatts in January 2026. Clean technology exports have grown to nearly 1.8 times their 2020 levels.

Canada still faces challenges meeting emissions targets

However, not every indicator is moving in the right direction. The share of electricity generated from non-emitting sources fell six percentage points between August 2020 and August 2026.

Meanwhile, emissions increased slightly in 2025 before declining slightly during the first half of 2026, leaving Canada well short of its climate targets.

data.title: Zoox Expands to Downtown Vegas and the Arts District
data.description:
Zoox announced that it is expanding its robotaxi service area from the Vegas Strip to include Downtown Las Vegas and the Arts District. The new service area also extends their service hours, with robotaxi rides running from 6 am to 3 am daily.

The extension comes 14 months after its initial launch in 2025 in the city. At launch, Zoox focused rides on and around the Vegas Strip as the first fully autonomous ride-hailing service using purpose-built vehicles.

The company has worked with several properties to organize dedicated and branded Zoox drop-off and pick-up zones, making it easier to find your next ride. This includes the Sphere, T-Mobile Arena, Resorts World, AREA15 and the Henry Reid International Airport.

Outside these specific pick-up areas, users will use the FindMyZoox feature in the Zoox app, which allows you to identify your ride in busy areas. Your Zoox ride will use sound cues and distinctive lighting to help you find the vehicle, and it will also provide licence plate information for easy identification.

With service also expanding in San Francisco and launches planned in Austin, Miami, Houston, and San Diego, Zoox is expanding methodically, and it seems to be working well for the company.
